solutionSql:
CREATE TABLE dim_customer (
  customer_key integer GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_name text NOT NULL UNIQUE
);
CREATE TABLE dim_route (
  route_key integer GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  origin text NOT NULL,
  destination text NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (origin, destination)
);
CREATE TABLE fact_shipment (
  tracking_code text PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_key integer NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_customer (customer_key),
  route_key integer NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_route (route_key),
  weight_kg integer,
  status text NOT NULL,
  booked_at timestamptz NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO dim_customer (customer_name)
SELECT DISTINCT customer_name
FROM staging_shipments_flat
WHERE customer_name IS NOT NULL;
INSERT INTO dim_route (origin, destination)
SELECT DISTINCT origin, destination
FROM staging_shipments_flat
WHERE origin IS NOT NULL AND destination IS NOT NULL;
INSERT INTO fact_shipment (tracking_code, customer_key, route_key, weight_kg, status, booked_at)
SELECT s.tracking_code, c.customer_key, r.route_key, s.weight_kg, s.status, s.booked_at
FROM staging_shipments_flat AS s
JOIN dim_customer AS c ON c.customer_name = s.customer_name
JOIN dim_route AS r ON r.origin = s.origin AND r.destination = s.destination;
sampleFirstRows: dim_customer: 6 rows (Aster Loomworks, Brindle Pantry, ...); dim_route: 4 rows
fact_shipment: 60 rows, one per tracking_code, with 3 weight_kg NULL
sampleChecks: On sample: dim_customer 6 rows, dim_route 4 rows, fact_shipment 60 rows (one per tracking code, all 60 staging rows have a name, origin and destination). Every fact row joins to both dimensions. Weight is NULL on 3 fact rows. Counts on the other datasets: nulls 6/4/56, boundary 6/4/60, nulltext 6/4/56, which match the rows with a name, origin and destination.

rules.howSolved: The fact load inner-joins dim_customer on the name and dim_route on the origin and destination pair, so each fact row names its own customer and route rows.
customer_key and route_key are declared NOT NULL foreign keys, so each fact row has both keys.
dim_customer has customer_name UNIQUE and is loaded with SELECT DISTINCT, so each name is held once.
dim_route has UNIQUE (origin, destination) and is loaded with SELECT DISTINCT over the pair.
tracking_code is the fact table's PRIMARY KEY, and the flat extract has one row per tracking code.
weight_kg is a nullable integer and the fact load does not filter on it, so a missing weight keeps the row.
The route load filters out rows with a null origin or destination, and the inner join then drops those shipments from the fact.
The customer load filters out null names, and the inner join on customer_name drops those shipments from the fact.

ambiguities: 'generated primary key' does not say GENERATED ALWAYS or GENERATED BY DEFAULT. I chose ALWAYS.
The fact table's primary key is not stated. I made tracking_code the PRIMARY KEY because the wording says one row per tracking_code, and I added no surrogate fact key because none is named.

The types and NOT NULL flags on status and booked_at are not stated. I used text and timestamptz, matching the flat extract, with NOT NULL. The extract has no null status or booked_at on any of the four datasets I ran.
dim_route's column types are not stated. I used text for origin and destination, matching the flat extract.
The instructions do not state a surrogate key for dim_route beyond 'generated primary key', which I took to mean route_key as a generated identity column.
notes: Input carried rule text only, so rule entries are labelled r1 to r8 in declared order. Their declared ids were not visible to the blind solver and need mapping by the lead. Policy used: CreateStmt and InsertStmt only. Ran cleanly on sample, nulls, boundary and nulltext. All three tables and loads run in dependency order, dimensions before fact.
